text:
sam: Heads up — getting reports from EU customers that TLS handshakes intermittently return the default cert instead of the host cert. Started after yesterday's edge rollout. Customers see cert mismatch on api.redwood-inference.com :scream:

maria: noticed a spike in TLS-failures and 525-like errors around 09:12 UTC. We rolled an ALB ssl-policy update (enabled TLS1.3) at 09:08, small canary first. :thinking:

devin: any raw ALB logs? My 1st guess: ECH (Encrypted ClientHello) — if clients send an encrypted ClientHello the ALB can't read SNI, so it serves the default cert and downstream routing fails for SNI-based vhosts. Modern browsers started enabling ECH by default in some channels.

sam: log snippet from CloudWatch: ```
[ALB] 2026-01-27T09:12:14Z target=nginx-01 no-sni -> served-default-cert arn:aws:acm:...:certificate/abcd1234
[ALB] 2026-01-27T09:12:14Z client=54.72.11.2 protocol=HTTPS cipher=TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 sni=""
```

joel: confirmed with infra: AWS ALB does not inspect or terminate ECH; when ECH is present SNI is encrypted and the ALB will not see it. That yields a blank SNI field. Options: 1) terminate TLS at ALB and rely on host header (not possible if SNI is missing), 2) move to TCP/TLS passthrough (NLB) so backend handles TLS and SNI selection, 3) disable ECH at the client (not realistic), 4) give a fallback SAN on the default cert that covers the affected host as a short-term mitigation.

maya: operational tradeoffs: NLB passthrough removes ALB features we use (WAF, redirect, advanced routing). Also certs must be managed at the pod/nginx level or via ACM+backend termination. We'll need to evaluate cost & complexity. Adding SAN to default cert is fastest for immediate relief.

devin: suggested action plan:
- short-term: issue a new default cert that includes api.redwood-inference.com as SAN to stop user errors (fast, low risk)
- medium: create an NLB TCP passthrough target group in eu-west-1, route a small canary of affected CIDRs to it so backend nginx can select certs by SNI (preserves per-host certs)
- long-term: track cloud provider ECH support / decide on an edge architecture decision (ALB with ECH blindspot vs NLB passthrough + lost ALB features)

sam: I'll create the cert request and a canary ticket. Example k8s svc patch to create NLB TCP passthrough (AWS):
```yaml
# patch svc to use NLB + TCP backend protocol
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: model-api
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: "tcp"
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
    - port: 443
      targetPort: 8443
```
(we'll also create a target group with TLS disabled on ALB and let nginx handle TLS at 8443)

deploy-bot: Canary route created: svc/model-api -> nlb-canary-eu (canary=ech-nlb) :rocket:

maria: added Grafana panel to track TLS mismatch count and blank-sni events. Will alert if >5/min. Ping me when canary is live and I'll watch.

sam: thanks all. I'll post PRs for the cert and the svc patch, and we'll roll canary quietly. Will open a ticket to cloud for ECH timeline.

Note: leaving this thread pinned to the incident channel until canary stabilizes.
